signatures.name: Deathless Rage
signatures.target: Self.
signatures.duration: Rage until scene end or until ended; reprieve until the end of your next turn.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Maneuver · **Attribute:** None (no roll)

**Target / range / shape:** Self.

Enter a rage until the end of the scene. While raging, gain 1 Boon to attack rolls, 1 Bane to defense rolls, and physical resistance 1. You can end the rage at will. It also ends if you fall unconscious or enter Dying.

Once per scene, when damage would reduce you to 0 HP during this rage, remain at 1 HP. If you regain HP before the end of your next turn, the reprieve ends and you keep that HP. Otherwise, fall to 0 HP and begin Dying at the end of that turn. Further damage can still bring you to 0 during the reprieve. If you survive reaching 0, record a scar as usual.

**Duration:** Rage until scene end or until ended; reprieve until the end of your next turn.

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

Use this rage once per scene. If you also know Go Berserk or Pain Feeds the Fire, all share that rage use. Pain Feeds the Fire’s damage-triggered Boon applies only if you also know that signature.

Otherwise, fall to 0 HP and begin Dying at the end of that turn. Further damage can still bring you to 0 during the reprieve. If you survive reaching 0, record a scar as usual.

**Duration:** Rage until scene end or until ended; reprieve until the end of your next turn.

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

Use this rage once per scene. If you also know Go Berserk or Pain Feeds the Fire, all share that rage use. Pain Feeds the Fire’s damage-triggered Boon applies only if you also know that signature.

signatures.name: Earthbreaker
signatures.target: Self; each enemy within 2 squares.
signatures.duration: Immediate.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** Brawn

**Target / range / shape:** Self; each enemy within 2 squares.

Make a Brawn roll and apply it to every enemy in range. Weak: 2 physical damage, and push 1 square directly away from you. Standard: 4 physical damage, push 2 squares, and it is Prone. Strong: 6 physical damage, push 3 squares, and it is Prone and Dazed 1. Structures and unattended objects in the area take double damage. Resolve collisions normally. This does not move you.

**Duration:** Immediate.

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

Use ordinary object HP, resistance and collision rules. Fixed barriers stop forced movement even if the damage breaks them.

**Frequency:** Once per scene.

signatures.name: The Cannonball
signatures.target: One creature within 4 squares.
signatures.duration: Immediate; Prone and Dazed use their normal rules.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** Brawn

**Target / range / shape:** One creature within 4 squares.

Move up to 4 squares in a straight line toward the target, ignoring difficult terrain. If you end adjacent to it, make a Brawn roll. Weak: 4 physical damage to the target. You take 3 physical damage and are Prone. Standard: 8 physical damage, and the target is Prone. You take 2 physical damage. Strong: 12 physical damage, and the target is Prone and Dazed 1. You take 1 physical damage and are Dazed 1. If you cannot move at least 2 squares, you cannot use this ability. Resolve collisions normally.

**Duration:** Immediate; Prone and Dazed use their normal rules.

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

Use once per scene. Its self-inflicted damage is non-attack damage, reduced by matching resistance to a minimum of 0; it is not an HP payment. It cannot trigger Pain Feeds the Fire.

signatures.target: Self; one visible creature.
signatures.duration: Until you move.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.

signatures.name: Beast Speech
signatures.target: Self.
signatures.duration: The scene.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Maneuver · **Attribute:** None (no roll)

**Target / range / shape:** Self.

For the scene, you can speak with animals. You can ask questions and understand their replies, limited by what the animal has experienced and can understand. You gain 1 Boon to all rolls interacting with animals you are speaking with. This does not make an animal friendly or obedient, and does not compel it to act against its nature.

**Duration:** The scene.

**Equipment / acquisition:** A free hand for casting.

This is a spell costing 0 SP. Animals retain their motives and agency. A companion acquired through play uses its actual profile.

**Frequency:** Once per scene.

flavor: You learn to work with the wild rather than merely command it.

signatures.name: Mark the Quarry
signatures.target: One visible creature within 12 squares.
signatures.duration: One day.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** Agility

**Target / range / shape:** One visible creature within 12 squares.

Requires a ranged weapon and ammunition. Make a Basic Ranged attack as part of this action. After the attack resolves, the target is marked for one day with the glowing dust of a cave mushroom. While marked, you and each ally who can see it gain 2 Boons to any attack against it, ignore partial cover from it, and the target cannot hide. The mark deals no additional damage.

**Duration:** One day.

**Equipment / acquisition:** A ranged weapon and ammunition.

This ordinary mark is a physical luminous substance. An attack always applies it unless the target cannot be reached; damage immunity does not prevent marking. Cleaning it off takes 1 minute. Completely covering the mark suspends its visual benefits until exposed.

**Frequency:** Once between safe overnight rests.

signatures.name: Call the Wild
signatures.target: One willing wild companion arriving in a visible empty square within 6 squares.
signatures.duration: Indefinite companionship; summoning is immediate and requires no Sustain.
signatures.limits: One signature choice at each of levels 1, 3 and 7.
signatures.effect:
**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** None

**Target / range / shape:** One willing wild companion arriving in a visible empty square within 6 squares.

**Magic:** Spell · **SP:** 2

Once per scene, call your bonded companion with 2 SP. Its profile is: Size Medium; HP 16; Speed 6; physical resistance 1; Brawn +1, Fortitude +1, Agility +1, Guile 0, Knowledge −1, Reason 0; Stability 0. Its natural Main Action attack uses Brawn against an adjacent target for 2/4/6 physical damage; Strong also applies Prone. It has the ordinary movement and basic actions its body can perform. You control its rolls. Once on your turn, command it within 6 squares: your Main Action grants it one Main Action and movement; your Maneuver grants it one Maneuver and movement. It receives no separate combat turn and has no Reaction. Without a command it defends normally but takes no combat actions. It is a living creature, can heal, and uses the normal Dying rules at 0 HP. You can have one bonded companion. Further castings recall that same creature with its current HP and conditions; casting neither restores nor revives it. It remains when uncommanded. If it dies or is released, finding a new willing companion requires a safe overnight rest and the DA’s appropriate wilderness fiction; the bond, not each casting, determines the creature.

**Duration:** Indefinite companionship; summoning is immediate and requires no Sustain.

**Equipment / acquisition:** A free hand.

flavor: You learn to work with the wild rather than merely command it.

You can have one bonded companion. Further castings recall that same creature with its current HP and conditions; casting neither restores nor revives it. It remains when uncommanded. If it dies or is released, finding a new willing companion requires a safe overnight rest and the DA’s appropriate wilderness fiction; the bond, not each casting, determines the creature.

**Duration:** Indefinite companionship; summoning is immediate and requires no Sustain.

**Equipment / acquisition:** A free hand.

flavor: Grey skin, great watchful eyes and a quiet step beneath the weight of the world.

The ancestors of Deep Dwarves went farther down. Over long generations, the people of the depths became shorter and slighter than their surface cousins. Their skin ranges through shades of grey, and their large eyes gather the faint light of the underground. Narrow shoulders and economical movements suit passages where a broad surface dwarf would struggle.

Many are naturally shy. They watch before approaching, speak after listening and prefer a familiar companion to the attention of a crowded room. Reserve does not diminish curiosity, courage or conviction. A quiet Deep Dwarf may be the first to notice danger and the one who refuses to abandon a friend.

Stone, darkness and small changes in air or vibration shape their experience. Those raised above ground bring the same sensitive bodies to unfamiliar surroundings. No ancestral instinct supplies a map of tunnels they have never walked.

The Stone Tells You — You rest your palm against the floor and wait for the answering tread.
A Sense of Depth — You wake in the dark and know which wall lies beneath the mountain.
A Patient Breath — You slow your breathing while the others hurry through the stale passage.
Through the Narrow Places — You lower your head and slip beneath the fallen beam without breaking stride.

flavor: Tiny fey bodies, long lives and minds forever asking what else a thing could become.

Gnomes are fey creatures, smaller even than halflings, with deft hands, keen senses and an intelligence that can make a complicated device seem almost embarrassingly obvious. Their faces carry the expressions of long experience, however easily a stranger mistakes their stature for youth.

Some say the gnomes left the world of fairie to explore possibilities its inhabitants had overlooked. Others insist they were thrown out, and disagree enthusiastically about what invention caused the trouble. Gnomes tell both stories. Whether anyone remembers the whole truth is another question.

Inventing and tinkering delight many gnomes: an unfamiliar mechanism invites examination, an accepted limitation invites an experiment. Others apply that same searching intelligence to music, medicine, argument or the behavior of friends. A gnome does not inherit a workshop or a profession. Their fey nature and extraordinary mind travel with them wherever they grow up.

Small Target — You tuck yourself behind the low stone as the arrow strikes its edge.
Bright Idea — You draw three lines in the dust, add a spoon, and the answer takes shape.

flavor: Quick hands, shared effort and a future finally open to your own making.

Goblins are small, quick-bodied people with prominent ears and alert, expressive faces. For generations, orcs enslaved them, and outsiders learned to associate goblins with the cruelty of those who held them. Freedom did not immediately erase that reputation. It did give goblins the chance to build lives whose purpose was their own.

Many now seek a place through useful work, trade, exploration and the steady proof of being a reliable neighbor. Resourcefulness honed under deprivation can become skilled repair, careful husbandry or a gift for seeing value where others see rubbish. Cooperation can become friendship and enterprise rather than a necessity of survival.

A goblin adventurer may want to support a community, win recognition or simply discover what freedom feels like beyond familiar roads. Others were born free and have never seen an orc. Their ancestry carries a history; each goblin chooses what to make of the life ahead.

flavor: Quiet feet, a generous table and courage that surprises people who judge by height.

Halflings are small, compact people, larger than gnomes, with a gift for making limited space comfortable. Others often notice their height before noticing the person, a mistake a halfling may patiently correct or quietly put to use.

Hospitality and good company are familiar pleasures, but a generous table does not require an easy life. Courage can live beside trembling knees, a sharp tongue beside warm manners, and a taste for home beside an irresistible curiosity about the road. A halfling raised far from halfling communities brings their own customs to those possibilities.

flavor: Tall, strong and deliberate; a long life leaves room to consider every word.

High Elves are tall and strongly built, with pointed ears and the fine, angular facial structure that leads outsiders to call them kin to Wood Elves. They are a different ancestry. Beside a compact, restless Wood Elf, a High Elf has the presence of a standing stone: upright, composed and difficult to hurry.

Their long lives encourage a broad view of consequences. Many listen through an argument before speaking, practice a movement until it wastes no effort, or remember a slight long after its author has forgotten it. Confidence can harden into arrogance, especially when patience is mistaken for superior judgment. Others learn that living a long time is no guarantee of being right.

A High Elf might be a laborer, a wanderer or a scholar. Strength and deliberation belong to their physical and temperamental inheritance; wealth, titles and courtly manners depend on the life they have led.

flavor: Broad shoulders, patient hands and a home made where mountain meets open sky.

Long ago, dwarven peoples took different roads. Some built their halls within mountains opening onto the surface world. Others traveled deeper into the earth. Centuries of separation, perhaps much longer, have left their descendants visibly different.

Hill Dwarves are the broad, stocky surface people: solid limbs, strong backs, dense hair and faces weathered by forge heat, mountain wind or ordinary years of work. Their halls connect stone interiors to roads, daylight and neighboring communities. Deep Dwarves are their distant kin, but a stranger would seldom mistake one for the other.

Endurance, craft and a lasting memory are familiar expressions of Hill Dwarf identity. A remembered debt may be a kindness worth returning as readily as an injury worth answering. A dwarf need not live in a mountain, work a forge or keep a grudge; the same steady body can belong to a sailor, gardener or traveling musician.

flavor: Restless, adaptable and fiercely invested in a life that never feels long enough.

Humans have no single stature, complexion or way of making a home. A short life beside the elder peoples can give an ordinary season an urgent importance: learn the trade, mend the friendship, see what lies beyond the ridge. Some make roots; others make roads between the places they love.

Adaptability takes many forms. One human gathers languages and acquaintances; another learns by failing until a stubborn problem yields. Neither ambition nor restlessness is compulsory. A human hero may want a quiet life enough to undertake a dangerous journey to protect it.

Ingenuity — You look at what is available and build the tool you need.
The Impossible Streak — Someone says it cannot be done, and you hear a challenge.

flavor: Made for a purpose. Set adrift before you learned what it was.

Oath-Bound are constructs brought into existence by an oath holder. Each was made for a higher purpose and carries a destiny, yet begins their life without knowing what that purpose or destiny is. They have been given existence without an explanation: a ship set adrift, with neither a chart nor a remembered destination.

Their oath holder is the source of that existence. An Oath-Bound may recognize a name, a presence or a sign of the one who made them. Calling upon that connection can bring conviction, understanding or strength. The answer may feel intimate even when the being who gives it remains a mystery.

Life among other peoples gives them relationships, work and ambitions of their own. A journey might uncover why they were made, or simply teach them what they value while searching. The character’s choices belong to the player; their hidden purpose offers a mystery to discover together with the Dungeon Architect.

items: The Answering Voice — You reach toward the presence that made you, and certainty settles into your voice.

The Will That Made You — Something in you remembers that your work is unfinished.
A Hand on the Rudder — For a moment, the world is less bewildering and the next step feels clearer.

flavor: Long limbs, great hands and a world whose doorways rarely give you room.

Tallfolk stand well above most neighboring peoples. Long arms, powerful frames and large hands make their scale evident even when they sit quietly. A borrowed chair, a crowded wagon or a low lintel can demand more thought than a heavy load.

Some enjoy the attention their height brings; others become practiced at folding themselves out of the way. Their bodies offer reach and leverage, but neither strength nor stature decides their character. A Tallfolk healer may work with extraordinary gentleness, while a shy scholar learns to endure being the first person everyone notices.

Their origins and communities belong to the campaign. They need no named giant ancestor or distant kingdom to take their place beside other adventurers. Choose how your hero lives at this scale, and which of its advantages they have learned to use.

flavor: Short, dark-haired and quick; the next possibility is already tugging at your sleeve.

Wood Elves are shorter and more lightly built than High Elves, with dark hair, nimble limbs and expressive, angular faces. Similar ears and facial structures have given both peoples the name elf in other tongues. A Wood Elf watching a High Elf deliberate may wonder how anyone can bear to leave an interesting idea untried for so long.

Quick movement often accompanies quick feeling. Curiosity, anger and affection can arrive with equal force; many Wood Elves trust the first useful opening and discover its consequences afterward. Their rashness can become daring, and their impulsiveness can become generosity. Neither prevents a Wood Elf from learning patience or taking a promise seriously.

Their bodies lend themselves to balance and movement. Woodlands give those gifts abundant expression, but a Wood Elf raised among rooftops, ships or crowded streets remains a Wood Elf. Their community determines what those quick hands learn to do.

Dream beneath the Stars — Your body rests while part of you walks old paths.

basicActions.effect:
**Action:** Movement · **Attribute:** None — no roll

**Target / range / shape:** Self

Spend up to Speed in movement squares, split around your actions. Each normal square costs 1 movement and each difficult square costs 2. While Prone, crawl for 2 per normal square or 3 per difficult square. Straight and diagonal steps cost the same. You may cross an occupied square if its occupant is Prone. **Duration:** Instant

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** Brawn

**Target / range / shape:** An adjacent obstacle, grapple, or creature

Before rolling, choose to reduce an obstacle’s remaining strength, reduce your own Grappled rating, or push a creature. The DA establishes any obstacle target. At Grappled 3 or higher, escape requires release by a grappler or an outside intervention that breaks the hold.

- **Standard:** Add 2 progress, reduce Grappled by 2, or push 2 squares.
- **Strong:** Add 3 progress, reduce Grappled by 3, or push 3 squares.

**Stability:** apply it only to the push option, not obstacle progress or Grappled reduction.

**Duration:** Instant

**Equipment / acquisition:** None.

# Basic Ranged

*Shoot a visible creature within 12 squares. Roll Agility for 2/3/5 physical damage.*

## Rules

**Action:** Main Action · **Attribute:** Agility

**Target / range / shape:** One visible creature within 12 squares

Choose your target and make the attack. You can reach a target 13–18 squares away with 1 Bane on the attack, or 1 Boon to its defense if the target rolls. Use the printed outcomes if you have learned a technique that uses ranged weapons. Without that training, deal 1/1/2 physical damage.

- **Weak:** 2 physical damage.
- **Standard:** 3 physical damage.
- **Strong:** 5 physical damage.

**Duration:** Instant

**Equipment / acquisition:** Requires a ranged weapon, Bulk 1, and ammunition, Bulk 1; grants neither. Check ammunition after use.

---

**Tier / minimum level:** Universal · **DP:** Not purchased · **Requirements to learn:** None

**Type:** Attack

**Limits:** Repeatable; pay the action and any stated costs each use.

**ID:** basic-ranged
